title: Create your account and sign in
summary: Choose TommyTezos as the account name, create a password login, and return safely to the desktop.
steps: Open Create Account from the wtfOS sign-in screen.
Enter TommyTezos and choose a private password.
Confirm the password and create the account.
Return later with Log In and confirm the TommyTezos desktop opens.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I make a wtfOS account and sign in. First, I click Create Account and type TommyTezos for my username. Then I make a private password, type it again, and click Create Account. There it is! When I come back later, I use Log In with the same TommyTezos name and my password.
spokenSteps: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I make a wtfOS account and sign in.
First, I click Create Account and type TommyTezos for my username.
Then I make a private password, type it again, and click Create Account.
There it is! When I come back later, I use Log In with the same TommyTezos name and my password.

title: Find and open wtfOS tools
summary: Use the Start menu, task shortcuts, and Applications catalog to reach the tool you need.
steps: Sign in as TommyTezos and open the Stuffs menu.
Close and reopen Stuffs so the menu gesture is easy to recognize.
Choose Play, Create, Shop, Events, or Talk for a guided destination.
Use menu search when you already know the tool name.
Open Applications to see the wider catalog and availability state.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I find stuff in wtfOS. First, I click Stuffs down here. I open it, close it, and open it again so you can see exactly where it is. These big choices take me straight to Play, Create, Shop, Events, or Talk. If I already know an app's name, I type it into search. Applications shows me the whole catalog and which tools are ready for me.

title: Connect and prove a Tezos wallet
summary: Link a Tezos wallet to TommyTezos with a signed ownership challenge, then sync tokens and domains.
steps: Open Profile while signed in as TommyTezos.
In Linked Wallets, choose Connect wallet to link.
Select a Tezos wallet provider and approve the connection.
Sign the ownership message; this is not a token transfer.
Confirm the wallet appears in the linked-wallet table.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I prove that a Tezos wallet is mine. First, I open Profile and scroll down to Linked Wallets. I click Connect wallet to link, then pick the wallet app I actually use. My wallet asks me to sign an ownership message. I read it, make sure it isn't sending tez, and sign. Hey, it worked! My address shows up here, and wtfOS can sync my tokens, domains, balance, and activity.
spokenSteps: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I prove that a Tezos wallet is mine.
First, I open Profile and scroll down to Linked Wallets.
I click Connect wallet to link, then pick the wallet app I actually use.
My wallet asks me to sign an ownership message. I read it, make sure it isn't sending tez, and sign.
Hey, it worked! My address shows up here, and wtfOS can sync my tokens, domains, balance, and activity.

title: Connect and prove an Etherlink wallet
summary: Link Temple or MetaMask on Etherlink Mainnet while keeping the Tezos wallet session separate.
steps: Open Profile and find Etherlink Wallets.
Choose Connect Temple or Connect MetaMask.
Approve Etherlink Mainnet, chain ID 42793, in the wallet.
Choose Link Connected and sign the ownership message.
Confirm the EVM address and synced assets appear.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I connect an Etherlink wallet without messing up my Tezos connection. First, I open Profile and find Etherlink Wallets. I click Temple or MetaMask and check that the network says Etherlink Mainnet, chain I D forty-two thousand seven hundred ninety-three. Then I click Link Connected and sign the ownership message. Neat! My E V M address, balance, and indexed assets appear right here, and I can use Sync whenever I want a fresh scan.

First, I open Profile and find Etherlink Wallets.
I click Temple or MetaMask and check that the network says Etherlink Mainnet, chain I D forty-two thousand seven hundred ninety-three.
Then I click Link Connected and sign the ownership message.

title: Connect X to prove your social identity
summary: Verify the X account associated with TommyTezos and choose whether the handle is public.
steps: Open the Social section in TommyTezos Profile.
Enter the expected X handle, then choose Connect X.
Authorize the matching X account with the displayed identity scopes.
Return to Profile and confirm the Verified badge.
Choose whether the handle is public, then save social info.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I prove which X account is mine. First, I open Profile and find Social. I type the X handle I expect to connect, then click Connect X. On X, I double-check the signed-in account and approve the identity permission. When I come back, wtfOS says Verified. Then I choose whether my handle is public and click Save social info. That's it—my account is proved without sharing my X password with wtfOS.
spokenSteps: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I prove which X account is mine.
First, I open Profile and find Social.
I type the X handle I expect to connect, then click Connect X.
On X, I double-check the signed-in account and approve the identity permission. When I come back, wtfOS says Verified.
Then I choose whether my handle is public and click Save social info. That's it—my account is proved without sharing my X password with wtfOS.

title: Connect Discord to prove your social identity
summary: Authorize Discord for TommyTezos and control whether the verified username is public.
steps: Open the Social section in TommyTezos Profile.
Choose Connect Discord.
Review the Discord account and requested identity permission.
Return to Profile and confirm the Verified badge.
Set the Public option and save social info.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I connect Discord to wtfOS. First, I open Profile, find Social, and click Connect Discord. Discord shows me the account and the identity permission wtfOS is asking for. I check that it's really mine and authorize it. Back in Profile, I look for the Verified badge. Then I choose whether the username is public and click Save social info. If I disconnect later, it only removes the link—it doesn't delete either account.

title: Connect Bluesky through Skywire
summary: Attach an AT Protocol identity to TommyTezos and choose the Skywire interaction tier.
steps: From TommyTezos Profile, choose Connect Skywire.
Enter the Bluesky handle or DID you control.
Choose the minimum Skywire permission tier that supports your intended actions.
Approve the AT Protocol authorization.
Return to Skywire and confirm the connected handle.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I connect my Bluesky identity through Skywire. First, I open Skywire's account screen and type the Bluesky handle or D I D I control. I pick the smallest permission level that can do what I want. Then I continue to Bluesky, check the exact account, and approve it. When Skywire comes back, there it is—my handle is connected to TommyTezos. I can upgrade permissions later or disconnect the link from Profile.

First, I open Skywire's account screen and type the Bluesky handle or D I D I control.
I pick the smallest permission level that can do what I want.
Then I continue to Bluesky, check the exact account, and approve it.
When Skywire comes back, there it is—my handle is connected to TommyTezos. I can upgrade permissions later or disconnect the link from Profile.

title: Connect Google Drive for Studio and My Media
summary: Use one private Drive connection for new Studio projects and automatic My Media upload backups.
steps: Open Studio as TommyTezos and find Your Drive.
Choose Connect Google Drive and select the Google account you control.
Approve the limited drive.file permission.
Return to Studio and confirm Connected status.
Open My Videos to confirm new uploads will also receive a Drive backup.
narration: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I connect my own cloud storage to wtfOS. First, I open Studio, find Your Drive, and click Connect Google Drive. I pick my Google account and review the limited drive dot file permission. That lets wtfOS use files it creates without browsing my whole Drive. When I come back, Studio says Connected. Now new projects can use my Drive, and My Videos can make an account-owned backup while wtfOS keeps the playback copy ready.
spokenSteps: Hi, I'm Tommy. Today I'm gonna show you how I connect my own cloud storage to wtfOS.
First, I open Studio, find Your Drive, and click Connect Google Drive.
I pick my Google account and review the limited drive dot file permission. That lets wtfOS use files it creates without browsing my whole Drive.
When I come back, Studio says Connected.
Now new projects can use my Drive, and My Videos can make an account-owned backup while wtfOS keeps the playback copy ready.
